Remote DuckDB

Source: vignettes/duckdb.Rmd
duckdb.Rmd

DuckDB is an analytical SQL database, often used to query data inside R. If you want several app users to query a shared remote database, you can run DuckDB as a server using Quack, its network protocol.

oauth_db_duckdb() connects your Shiny app to that server with each visitor’s access token. You query with DBI or dbplyr, while the server checks the token and controls access. This setup needs a remote server configured for OAuth; opening a local DuckDB file doesn’t provide user sign-in.

Try the local Quack demo

With Docker running, launch the configured server and Shiny app:

shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo("duckdb")

Sign in as Alice or Bob using the demo accounts. Both can read the shared sample table. Try a write checks that the server rejects writes. Docker supplies the matching DuckDB client and server extensions. See ?oauth_db_demo for editing the app or copying the server configuration.

Before running the app

You need a Quack server configured to accept OAuth access tokens and a matching DuckDB client. Install R’s duckdb package (1.5.3 or later) with the quack and httpfs extensions; installation steps follow the app.

Setting Where to get it
host, port The remote Quack server or its TLS proxy
Table name A table in the remote catalog the visitor can read
Issuer, client ID, secret Your app registration with the server’s trusted provider
quack:read The default read scope; use your server’s scope if it differs
ca_bundle, if needed The CA certificate for a privately signed server certificate

Register http://localhost:8100 as the redirect URI. Configure the provider to issue the server’s audience and read scope, then save the registration in .Renviron and restart R:

OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
OAUTHDB_DUCKDB_ISSUER=https://login.example.org/realms/reporting

A complete app

Replace the hostname, port and table name for your deployment. This example uses port 443 for a TLS proxy; Quack’s default port is 9494.

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_DUCKDB_ISSUER")
)
client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "quack:read")
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_duckdb(
    auth$connection,
    host = "duckdb.example.org",
    port = 443,
    required_scopes = "quack:read"
  )
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT * FROM orders LIMIT 20")
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at http://localhost:8100
# (viewers in RStudio/Positron/etc. cannot perform necessary redirects)

Run source("example.R"). The app waits for sign-in before connecting and clears the output on sign-out. Get a connection inside each render or reactive expression before running queries.

For dbplyr, use dplyr::tbl(con(), "orders"). The helper attaches the remote catalog as oauth_remote and selects its main schema. Pass schema to select another remote schema. Table queries use the attached catalog; standalone expressions such as SELECT current_user can run locally and do not prove which remote principal the server authenticated.

Install extensions and prepare the server

Use compatible DuckDB and Quack versions on the client and server. Install the client extensions before running the Shiny app:

install.packages("duckdb")
connection <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = ":memory:")
DBI::dbExecute(connection, "INSTALL quack")
DBI::dbExecute(connection, "INSTALL httpfs")
DBI::dbDisconnect(connection, shutdown = TRUE)

Keep the extensions in a directory the app can use across R sessions, using DUCKDB_EXTENSION_DIRECTORY if needed.

On the server, configure an OAuth validator such as quack_oauth. Set its trusted issuer and audience, and define the scopes and data access policy for your users. Quack’s shared-token check alone doesn’t validate OAuth tokens. Only the server needs the validator; shinyOAuth handles browser sign-in and token renewal in the app.

Expose the server through TLS with a certificate the client trusts. Pass ca_bundle for a private CA. See Quack security and ?oauth_db_duckdb for connection options, including local development.

Connection lifetime

Call con() before each operation. Quack receives a token when connecting, so the helper replaces the connection after token renewal. This ends transactions and discards temporary client state. Keep a transaction within one operation and get a current connection for the next one.

Signing out, changing accounts or ending the Shiny session closes the connection. The helper doesn’t retry SQL or replay transactions. If connection setup fails, check the endpoint, certificate, token audience and scopes with the server administrator.

For several accounts and saved results, see Getting started.
